summary: The University of Sydney publishes a two-lane assessment model in which unit instructions and supervised-assessment rules determine when AI may be used.

dimensions.summary: Sydney's open-assessment approach permits AI unless a unit coordinator says otherwise, while assessment procedures identify the permitted tools and acknowledgement method.

do: Check the unit outline and coordinator's AI instructions for the assessment.
dont: Do not treat the open-assessment approach as permission for every task.

dimensions.summary: Supervised examinations and supervised in-semester tests are excluded from Sydney's described default, so their own instructions control.

do: Check whether the assessment is supervised and follow its specific instructions.
dont: Do not carry the open-assessment rule into a supervised exam or test.

dimensions.summary: Sydney says students who use AI in assessments must acknowledge it, including generative translation, paraphrasing, and referencing tools.

do: Acknowledge every AI tool used in an assessment as required by the course.
dont: Do not submit AI-assisted assessment work without acknowledgement.

dimensions.summary: Sydney's guardrails say confidential, personal, proprietary, and other sensitive information should not be entered into AI tools.

do: Keep confidential and sensitive information out of AI tools.
dont: Do not enter personal or proprietary information into an AI prompt.

dimensions.summary: Sydney provides students free access to Microsoft Copilot for Web and recommends university-endorsed protected mode, but access is not assessment permission.

do: Use the university login and protected mode described by Sydney when choosing Copilot.
dont: Do not treat Copilot access as permission in coursework or exams.

dimensions.summary: No research or publication rule is included in this snapshot.
